prerequisites: Solid knowledge of school mathematics including grade 11, especially: arithmetic operations with real numbers (fractions, powers, roots, logarithms)
Familiarity with algebraic calculation rules, confident manipulation of equations and inequalities, term transformations
Solution of linear and quadratic equations
Introductory knowledge of elementary real functions, their graphs and typical properties
More important than detailed knowledge is practiced and confident handling of elementary methods of school mathematics (calculation techniques and methodological understanding)

learning_outcomes.text: Students possess broad foundational knowledge of mathematical methods relevant to engineering and computer science.
Students can name mathematical solution procedures.
Students can characterize and differentiate the application areas of mathematical methods in engineering problems.
Students are aware of the prerequisites for using the methods.
Students can compare mathematical procedures in engineering and computer science and apply them in a problem-oriented way.
Students can analyze and solve simple subject-specific problems using mathematical methods.
Students are able to proceed in a structured and methodical way when creating solutions.

syllabus_topics: Differential calculus for functions of one variable
assessment_rules: The portfolio exam is worth 100 points and consists of a two-hour written exam (K2) and a written work sample (APS). A maximum of 80 points can be achieved with the K2. The APS is offered twice, students are free to participate in both written work samples. The best-rated written work sample, with a maximum of 20 points, will be included in the evaluation.
